doc.citation: Molyneux, S. G., Barron, H. F. & Smith, R. A. (2008). Upper Llandovery–Wenlock (Silurian) palynology of the Pentland Hills inliers, Midland Valley of Scotland. Scottish Journal of Geology 44(2), 151–168. [Bibliographic record](https://nora.nerc.ac.uk/id/eprint/5279/).
doc.comment: Acritarchs were the main focus. The entire supplied text and captions were read. The accompanying manuscript PDF clips Figures 5–7, preventing complete recovery of sample-level spore assignments and counts; readable Figure 8 supplies formation-level lists. Formation summaries and separately reported samples overlap and must not be counted as independent assemblages. The Henshaw list combines this study with Wellman & Richardson (1993), Terrestrial plant microfossils from Silurian inliers of the Midland Valley of Scotland; Knockgardner records derive from Dorning (1982), Early Wenlock acritarchs from the Knockgardner and Straiton Grit Formations of Knockgardner, Ayrshire. Henshaw dating is spore-based. Question marks in Figure 8 occurrence cells are recorded as qualifiers without inserting them into the printed taxon labels. British National Grid references are retained in locality fields; no latitude or longitude is supplied.

items.locality: Pentland Hills, Midland Valley of Scotland
items.section_or_core: North Esk, Bavelaw Castle and Loganlee inliers
items.age_basis_detail: Graptolite dating attributed to Bull & Loydell (1995) and Loydell (2005); acritarch assemblages are consistent with late Llandovery.
items.notes: Figure 8 pools the Pentland Hills records. Acritarchs comprise more than 90% of each productive North Esk Reservoir assemblage. Cryptospores occur consistently in low numbers in the highest four North Esk samples, MPA 43843, 43296, 43847 and 43846. Alternative environmental interpretations are a deep-water submarine fan and a shallow-water shelf; redistribution or resedimentation of palynomorphs in turbidites is discussed without demonstrating older reworked spores. The tentative dyad identification is indicated by a question mark in Figure 8.

items.locality: Lynslie Burn, North Esk Inlier, Pentland Hills
items.age_basis_detail: Explicitly dated on spore evidence from Wellman & Richardson (1993); no named spore zone is given here.
items.setting_as_reported: a terrestrial alluvial fan complex with minor marine incursions
items.notes: Figure 8 combines this paper and Wellman & Richardson (1993), so individual taxa cannot all be attributed to the new samples. New productive exposures lie close to the earlier study's samples and yield closely similar assemblages. Spores and cryptospores are more abundant and diverse than below; rare marine acritarchs and associated plant material also occur. Rimosotetras problematica is tentative in the occurrence cell.
items.locator: Figure 8 and its caption; manuscript pp. 5, 8

items.age_basis_detail: Formation-level age based on graptolites; no direct dating of this sample is reported.
items.notes: The only productive sample among six Loganlee samples yielded sparse marine palynomorphs and cryptospore tetrads. Preservation may have been affected by intrusion of the Black Hill Felsite. Sample number cannot be recovered from the clipped figures. This record overlaps the pooled Reservoir formation summary.
items.locator: Manuscript p. 9, Bavelaw Castle and Loganlee inliers; Figure 7

items.notes: Spot sample rather than part of a systematically sampled section. Abundant, well-preserved acritarchs accompany rarer cryptospores, chitinozoans and scolecodonts. items.age_basis_detail: Assemblage resembles those of the Drumyork Flags and upper Reservoir formations. Figure 8 incorporates records probably, rather than certainly, from the Drumyork Flags; no independent sample age is supplied.
items.notes: Formation assignment is uncertain. Abundant acritarchs occur with rarer chitinozoans, scolecodonts and cryptospores. Despite lacking Moyeria, the assemblage strongly resembles Drumyork Flags and upper Reservoir microfloras.
